subject: Throughput & latency synthesis — next steps for p95/p99 qualification
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency synthesis — p95/p99 qualification next steps

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the p95/p99 qualification for the hosted evaluation vs your current provider.

Recap (from the call)
- Target E2E SLOs: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms for small-text generation paths (avg payload ~1.2KB).
- Streaming use-case: incremental response streaming for chat; typical chunk size ~600 bytes, client expects first-chunk within 80ms for interactive flows.
- Concurrency profile: peak 250 concurrent sessions, steady-state 70-90 concurrent; burst to 600 for short windows.
- Throughput: baseline 120 req/s, target 300 req/s sustained for scale test.

What we need from Acme to scope the POC (please reply with the attached spreadsheet if possible):
1) Traffic profile: per-endpoint RPS by minute, payload size distribution (we attached a template).
2) Exact p95/p99 targets by endpoint (chat vs batch generation).
3) Any cold-start / warm-cache expectations (warm vs cold KV cache hit rates).
4) Typical session lengths and KV cache reuse patterns for streaming.

Proposed POC plan (high level)
- Phase 1 (day 1–3): ingest traffic profile + run synthetic replay with 1:1 mapping to your production payloads. Measure p95/p99 under controlled concurrency (70, 250, 600).
- Phase 2 (day 4–7): streaming envelope tests — measure first-chunk latency and tail under continuous streaming (concurrency + batching).
- Phase 3 (day 8–10): production-mirroring run for final acceptance; compare hosted results to your incumbent numbers.

Actions / owners
- Kimberly (me): coordinate scheduling, contract/config for hosted trial, confirm metrics and SLIs.
- Rishi (cc): will own runtime config and test harness.
- Laura (cc): will handle SLO reporting dashboards and SLA mapping.

Attachments: perf_requirements_template.xlsx — please fill out and return.

Can you confirm target dates for the POC window next week and send the traffic CSV? We’ll provision a capacity profile matching your peak burst pattern for the first run.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

[Attachment: perf_requirements_template.xlsx]

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@acme.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency synthesis — p95/p99 qualification next steps

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the detailed recap and the template. Quick answers and attached a preliminary traffic dump (acme_traffic_profile.csv).

Data points:
- Baseline avg payload (generation request body): 1.1KB; responses vary widely but we’ll provide distribution in CSV.
- Streaming behavior: "chat" endpoint streams partial tokens; first-byte for ~70% of sessions is within 50-90ms today; tail p99 often spikes when our incumbent vendor autoscaling fires.
- Current provider numbers (incumbent): p95 ~115ms (good), p99 ~420ms in our peak windows — causes are often cold-start + KV cache miss after deployments.
- Concurrency: steady ~80 concurrent, peak sustained 240 during promotions; short spikes to ~700 for <2min when we run marketing bursts.
- Warm-cache expectation: we expect >85% KV reuse for chat (session-affinity helps).

Questions for Redwood:
1) How do you measure p99 for streaming sessions (end-to-end vs token-level)? We need end-to-end p99 on first-chunk and final-chunk.
2) For the POC, can you provision a warm cache baseline (simulate our cache hit rate) or do you require cold starts to validate?

We’ll return the completed CSV by EOD. Looking at availability — we can target a POC window next Tue–Thu (Apr 6–8).

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme AI

[Attachment: acme_traffic_profile.csv]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency synthesis — p95/p99 qualification next steps

Kimberly / team — reading Tom’s numbers, a few quick technical clarifications and a proposed test-run configuration:

Technical clarifications we’ll need from Acme (can ask them to mark in the CSV):
- Per-endpoint concurrency breakdown (chat ingestion vs generation) so we can map batching windows.
- Session-affinity TTL for KV cache (how long a session keeps the same KV routing key).
- Expected token rates per session for streaming — needed to size our prefetch/batching knobs.

Proposed test harness config for baseline runs (we’ll document this in the drive link):
- Instance profile: 4xA100-equivalent per shard, isolated for POC to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Batching strategy: adaptive batching with max-latency cap set to 25ms for interactive endpoints. This preserves p95 while allowing throughput headroom.
- KV cache warmup: run a 30-minute replay at 0.7x peak to pre-populate caches; then execute the official run. We should capture cache hit histogram and p95/p99 delta pre/post warmup.
- Streaming measurement: measure first-byte latency (from request ingest to first chunk emitted) and final-byte latency; both recorded as end-to-end. Also capture token-emission intervals for tail analysis.

I’ll prepare the harness and the perf dashboard templates (Grafana link below) — we should have a dry run on Apr 5 and full POC Apr 6–8 if Acme signs off.

Drive doc with runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-perf-POC
Grafana template: https://internal.redwood.com/dashboards/ACME-POC-template

Rishi

rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Tom — perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV. Confirming next steps and commitments:

1) POC schedule: we’ll do a dry run Apr 5 (internal only), then the three-day POC Apr 6–8 as you suggested. Please consider Apr 6 as the primary test day for the spike/throughput runs.
2) Warm-cache: we will run the 30-minute warmup prior to each official run to emulate your 85% KV reuse expectation. We’ll publish cache-hit histograms in the post-run report.
3) Metrics we’ll deliver: end-to-end p95/p99 for first-chunk and final-chunk, per-endpoint throughput (RPS), concurrency envelope, KV hit-rate, and cost-per-token estimate for the test profile.
4) Contacts & escalation:
   - Redwood SRE & lead: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai (runtime config, test harness)
   - Redwood PM/console: laura.bennett@redwood.ai (dashboards & metrics)
   - Contract/sales: aditya.rao@redwood.ai (trial terms & billing guardrails)
5) Docs & access: we’ll upload the test harness results to the Drive folder (link below) and create a shared Grafana view.

Please reply with a preferred time for a 30-min kickoff on Apr 5 to walk through the exact traffic replay steps. Once we have the filled CSV we’ll provision capacity and share the public endpoints for your infra to sanity-check.

Thanks again — looking forward to running this.

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
